title: TaskResult
description:
Structured result produced by an agent when output_format=structured. The runtime injects a closing instruction into the task prompt requiring the agent to emit this as a final fenced ```oap-result``` block. The runtime parses the block and uses it as the authoritative source for outputs, artifacts, and epoch coordination signals.

The fenced block contract:
  ```oap-result
  { "status": "ok", "outputs": {}, "artifacts": [], "build_ready": true }
  ```

Runtimes MUST:
  1. Append the oap-result instruction to the agent's task description.
  2. Parse the LAST oap-result block emitted (agents may emit intermediate drafts).
  3. Promote outputs[] scalars to signal.output envelopes.
  4. Promote artifacts[] paths to signal.artifact envelopes.
  5. Call epoch.MarkReady() if build_ready=true and a build_policy is defined.

status.description: Task completion status. 'ok' = success, all success_criteria met. 'error' = terminal failure, no usable output. 'partial' = work done but some criteria unmet (e.g. build still failing).

summary.description: Human-readable summary of what was accomplished. Runtime MAY surface this as the task's final log entry or as the agent's last signal.output text.

outputs.description: Named output values. Keys SHOULD match the task's declared outputs[]. Scalar values (string, number, boolean) are promoted to signal.output envelopes and become available via ${tasks.<name>.outputs.<key>} interpolation in downstream tasks. Nested objects and arrays are stored as-is and accessible but NOT promoted to individual envelopes.

artifacts.description: File paths written or modified by this task. Paths SHOULD be relative to the workflow's working_dir. Each path is promoted to a signal.artifact envelope and registered in the file registry for epoch attribution and parallel-write conflict detection. If the agent also emitted signal.artifact signals during streaming, the union of both lists is used.

build_ready.description: When true, the agent asserts that all file writes are complete and the codebase is ready for a build epoch. The runtime calls epoch.MarkReady() on the agent's behalf — equivalent to sending a build.ready message. Only meaningful when the workflow defines a build_policy. When build_ready=true the runtime does NOT need auto_ack=true on the build_policy.

error.description: Error description when status is 'error' or 'partial'. REQUIRED when status != 'ok'. Should include enough context for the coordinator to decide whether to retry, escalate, or fail the workflow.

additional_tasks.description: Continuation tasks the agent wants added to the DAG. Each task is validated (known agents, no cycles, valid deps referencing existing or sibling tasks) and inserted into the live graph. Only processed when status is 'ok' or 'partial'. Runtimes MUST validate continuation tasks before adding them. If validation fails, the runtime MUST log the error and skip the invalid tasks (the parent task still completes normally).

tokens_used.description: Self-reported token usage for this task. Runtime MAY prefer its own tracked values from the transport layer if available; this field is a fallback for runtimes that don't track tokens independently.
